item.title: Avraham Is Your Father: The Rambam's Letters to Ovadia the Convert
item.description:
Can a convert say "God of our fathers"? The Rambam's answers to Ovadia the convert: Avraham is your father, marriage is not predetermined, and how he regarded Islam.
Part of Dayan Daniel Kada's Tuesday-night series on the Rambam's letters (Igrot HaRambam), given on Zoom, January to April 2025.

item.title: Are We Ruled by the Stars? The Rambam's Letter on Astrology, Part 1
item.description:
Why did the Rambam call astrology a disease? His letter to the sages of Montpellier: believe only what reason, the senses or prophecy establish, and why relying on the stars cost Israel its kingdom.
Part of Dayan Daniel Kada's Tuesday-night series on the Rambam's letters (Igrot HaRambam), given on Zoom, January to April 2025.

item.title: Torah in Any Language, Resurrection & Custom: The Rambam's Letter to Yosef Ibn Jabbar
item.description:
A man who called himself ignorant asks the Rambam about resurrection and custom. The answer: learn Torah in any language you understand, physical resurrection is a fundamental, and a mistaken custom does not bind.
Part of Dayan Daniel Kada's Tuesday-night series on the Rambam's letters (Igrot HaRambam), given on Zoom, January to April 2025.

item.title: Should Forced Converts Be Condemned? The Rambam's Letter on Martyrdom, Part 1
item.description:
May a Jew forced to declare Muhammad a prophet be called a heretic? The Rambam's early Letter on Martyrdom takes apart a rabbi who condemned the forced converts, and shows that Jews who complied under duress were never rejected.
Part of Dayan Daniel Kada's Tuesday-night series on the Rambam's letters (Igrot HaRambam), given on Zoom, January to April 2025.

item.title: Forced to Convert: Live, Keep the Misvot and Leave | The Rambam's Letter on Martyrdom, Part 4
item.description:
What should a Jew do when forced only to say words? The Rambam's ruling: acknowledge rather than die, keep every misvah you can, and leave; and those who sin under persecution must be embraced, not rejected.
Part of Dayan Daniel Kada's Tuesday-night series on the Rambam's letters (Igrot HaRambam), given on Zoom, January to April 2025.

item.title: Even Hillel Would Have Been Angry | The Rambam's Letter to Rav Pinehas HaDayyan, Part 1
item.description:

item.title: Why No Names, No Sources in the Mishneh Torah? | The Rambam's Letter to Rav Pinehas HaDayyan, Part 2
item.description:
Why does the Mishneh Torah give no names and no sources? The Rambam explains that he wrote a composition like the Mishnah, not a commentary like the Talmud, and that the Talmud must still be studied.

item.title: "He Knows Nothing"? Rulings & Rumours | The Rambam's Letter to Rav Pinehas HaDayyan, Part 3
